content.title: About
content.content: A hamburger is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a medium beef patty placed between a soft wheat bun. It is often served with lettuce, tomato, onion, cheese, sauces, and pickles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first hamburger was served in the United States in the late 19th century.
The name “hamburger” comes from the German city of Hamburg, where similar meat patties were popular.
Hamburgers gained massive popularity among American soldiers during World War II.
There are more than 300 hamburger variations, including vegetarian and vegan versions.
The world’s largest hamburger weighed over 1 ton.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Hamburgers supply B12, B6, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is important for immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of protein, fat, and carbohydrates provides quick energy.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Salt and sauces
items.content: Large amounts of salt and sauces can increase the risk of hypertension.

items.title: Caloric content
items.content: Hamburgers are calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The bun contains gluten, and toppings may include dairy, which is relevant for people with allergies.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hamburgers are typically eaten by hand, holding them with both hands. You can add fresh vegetables, cheese, avocado, or swap heavy sauces for lighter options.

content.title: Storage
content.content: A prepared hamburger can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. The patty can be frozen for up to 3 months, and the bun should be stored in a dry place protected from moisture.
